arxiv-2006-05627.title: A survey on deep supervised hashing methods for image retrieval
arxiv-2006-05627.creator: Xiaopeng Zhang
arxiv-2006-05627.description: Abstract Hashing has been widely used in approximate nearest search for large-scale database retrieval for its computation and storage efficiency.Deep hashing, which devises convolutional neural network architecture to exploit and extract the semantic information or feature of images, has received increasing attention recently.

arxiv-2103-16564.title: Grounding Physical Concepts of Objects and Events Through Dynamic Visual Reasoning
arxiv-2103-16564.creator: Zhenfang Chen, Jiayuan Mao, Jiajun Wu, Kwan-Yee K. Wong, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, Chuang Gan
arxiv-2103-16564.description: Abstract We study the problem of dynamic visual reasoning on raw videos. This is a challenging problem; currently, state-of-the-art models often require dense supervision on physical object properties and events from simulation, which are impractical to obtain in real life.

arxiv-2105-03454.title: A Bayesian Gaussian Process for Estimating a Causal Exposure Response Curve in Environmental Epidemiology
arxiv-2105-03454.creator: Boyu Ren, Xiao Wu, Danielle Braun, Natesh Pillai, Francesca Dominici
arxiv-2105-03454.description: Abstract Motivated by environmental policy questions, we address the challenges of estimation, change point detection, and uncertainty quantification of a causal exposure-response function (CERF). Under a potential outcome framework, the CERF describes the relationship between a continuously varying exposure (or treatment) and its causal effect on an outcome.

arxiv-2210-01563.title: Calculation of mass and width of unstable molecular state using the developed Bethe-Salpeter theory
arxiv-2210-01563.creator: Xiaozhao Chen, Xiaofu Lü, Xiurong Guo, Zonghua Shi, Qingbiao Wang
arxiv-2210-01563.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xiaozhao Chen, Xiaofu Lü, Xiurong Guo, Zonghua Shi, Qingbiao Wang. Applying the developed Bethe-Salpeter theory for dealing with resonance, we investigate the time evolution of molecular state composed of two vector mesons as determined by the total Hamiltonian.

arxiv-2308-02634.title: Contrast Loss from Astrophysical Backgrounds in Space-Based Matter-Wave Interferometers
arxiv-2308-02634.creator: Yufeng Du, Clara Murgui, Kris Pardo, Yikun Wang, Kathryn M. Zurek
arxiv-2308-02634.description: Abstract Atom and matter interferometers are precise quantum sensing experiments that can probe differential forces along separated spacetime paths. Various atom and matter interferometer experiments have been proposed to study dark matter, gravitational waves, and exotic new physics. Increasingly, these experimental concepts have proposed space-based designs to maximize interrogation times and baselines.

arxiv-2311-16299.title: Manipulating the Stacking in Two-Dimensional Hexagonal Boron Nitride Bilayers: Implications for Defect-Based Single Photon Emitters
arxiv-2311-16299.creator: Fernanda Pinilla, Wilver A. Muriel, Javiera Cabezas-Escares, Ignacio Chacón, Carlos Cardenas, Francisco Munoz
arxiv-2311-16299.description: Abstract Defect-based single photon emitters are a very interesting option for quantum technologies. Unlike bulk-based emitters, two-dimensional materials provide advantages, such as the possibility of forming van der Waals heterostructures. In them, the adjacent layers can be used to control or modify some properties, often in a controlled way.

arxiv-2312-14683.title: The XXL survey LII : The evolution of radio AGN luminosity function determined via parametric methods from GMRT, ATCA, VLA and Cambridge interferometer observations
arxiv-2312-14683.creator: B. Šlaus, V. Smolčić, Ž. Ivezić, S. Fotopoulou, C. J. Willott, P. Pendo, C. Vignali, L. Chiappetti, M. Pierre
arxiv-2312-14683.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by B. Šlaus, V. Smolčić, Ž. Ivezić, S. Fotopoulou, C. J. Willott, P. Pendo, C. Vignali, L. Chiappetti, M. Pierre. We model the evolution of active galactic nuclei by constructing their radio luminosity functions. We use a set of surveys of varying area and depth, namely the deep COSMOS survey of 1,916 1,916 AGN sources, the wide shallow 3CRR, 7C and 6CE surveys, containing together 356 356 AGNs, and the intermediate XXL-North and South fields consisting of 899 899 and 1,484 1,484 sources, respectively.

arxiv-2401-16206.title: On the James brace product: Generalization, relation to H H -splitting of loop space fibrations & the J J -homomorphism
arxiv-2401-16206.creator: Somnath Basu, Aritra Bhowmick, Sandip Samanta
arxiv-2401-16206.description: Abstract . Given a fibration F ↪ E → B F\hookrightarrow E\rightarrow B with a homotopy section s : B → E s:B\rightarrow E , James introduced a binary product { , } s : π i B × π j F → π i + j − 1 F \left\{,\right\}_{s}:\pi_{i}B\times\pi_{j}F\rightarrow\pi_{i+j-1}F , called the brace product.

arxiv-2406-11491.title: Freely Decaying Saffman Turbulence Experimentally Generated by Magnetic Stirrers
arxiv-2406-11491.creator: Jean-Baptiste Gorce, Eric Falcon
arxiv-2406-11491.description: Abstract We investigate experimentally the decay of three-dimensional hydrodynamic turbulence, initially generated by the erratic motions of centimeter-size magnetic stirrers in a closed container. Such zero-mean-flow homogeneous isotropic turbulence is well suited to test Saffman’s model and Batchelor’s model of freely decaying turbulence.

arxiv-2406-17123.title: Bidimensional Exploration of the warm-Temperature Ionised gaS (BETIS)
arxiv-2406-17123.creator: R. González-Díaz, F. F. Rosales-Ortega, L. Galbany
arxiv-2406-17123.description: Abstract The extraplanar diffuse ionised gas (eDIG) is a key component for understanding the feedback processes that connect galactic discs and their halos. In this paper, we present the second study of the Bidimensional Exploration of the warm-Temperature Ionised Gas (BETIS) project, which aims to explore the possible ionisation mechanisms and characteristics of the eDIG.

arxiv-2503-12858.title: Harnessing Test-time Adaptation for NLU tasks Involving Dialects of English
arxiv-2503-12858.creator: Duke Nguyen, Aditya Joshi, Flora Salim
arxiv-2503-12858.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Duke Nguyen, Aditya Joshi, Flora Salim. Test-time adaptation (TTA) is an excellent method which helps generalize models across domains, tasks, and distributions without the use of labeled datasets. Thus, TTA is very useful in natural language processing (NLP) in the dialectal setting, since oftentimes, models are trained on Standard American English (SAE), evaluated on Indian English or Nigerian English, of which distribution differs significantly from the former. This is especially useful since dialectal datasets are scarce.

arxiv-2505-11729.title: Neural Importance Sampling of Many Lights 1339 Journal: TOG Conference: Special Interest Group on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques Conference Conference Papers ; August 10–14, 2025; Vancouver, BC, Canada Special Interest Group on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques Conference Co
arxiv-2505-11729.creator: Pedro Figueiredo, Qihao He, Steve Bako, Nima Khademi Kalantari
arxiv-2505-11729.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Pedro Figueiredo, Qihao He, Steve Bako, Nima Khademi Kalantari. We propose a neural approach for estimating spatially varying light selection distributions to improve importance sampling in Monte Carlo rendering, particularly for complex scenes with many light sources. Our method uses a neural network to predict the light selection distribution at each shading point based on local information, trained by minimizing the KL-divergence between the learned and target distributions in an online manner.

arxiv-2506-06252.title: Lightweight Prompt Biasing for Contextualized End-to-End ASR Systems
arxiv-2506-06252.creator: Bo Ren, Yu Shi, Jinyu Li
arxiv-2506-06252.description: Abstract End-to-End Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) has advanced significantly yet still struggles with rare and domain-specific entities. This paper introduces a simple yet efficient prompt-based biasing technique for contextualized ASR, enhancing recognition accuracy by leverage a unified multi-task learning framework.

arxiv-2507-00941.title: Seeing is not believing in limited visibility cops and robbers
arxiv-2507-00941.creator: Bojan Bašić ✉, Alfie Davies ✉ ​ {}^{\textrm{\hrefmailto:research@alfied.xyz}\,\,\raisebox{-0.60275pt}{\lx@orcidlink{0000-0002-4215-7343}{\orcidlogo}}\,}, Aleksa Džuklevski ✉, Strahinja Gvozdić ✉, Yannick Mogge ✉ ​ {}^{\textrm{\hrefmailto:yannick.mogge@univ-lyon1.fr}\,\,\raisebox{-0.60275pt}{\lx@orci
arxiv-2507-00941.description: Abstract We consider the model of limited visibility Cops and Robbers, where the cops can only see within their l l -neighbourhood. We prove that the number of cops needed to see the robber can be arbitrarily smaller than the number needed to capture the robber, answering an open question from the literature.

arxiv-2507-17211.title: EFS: Evolutionary Factor Searching for Sparse Portfolio Optimization Using Large Language Models
arxiv-2507-17211.creator: Haochen Luo, Yuan Zhang, Chen Liu
arxiv-2507-17211.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Haochen Luo, Yuan Zhang, Chen Liu. Sparse portfolio optimization is a fundamental yet challenging problem in quantitative finance, since traditional approaches heavily relying on historical return statistics and static objectives can hardly adapt to dynamic market regimes. To address this issue, we propose E volutionary F actor S earch ( EFS ), a novel framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to automate the generation and evolution of alpha factors for sparse portfolio construction.

plos-pone-0012175.description: PLOS ONE research article. RNA silencing is a common term for pathways utilizing small RNAs as sequence-specific guides to repress gene expression. Components of the RNA silencing machinery are involved in different aspects of chromatin function in numerous organisms. However, association of RNA silencing

pmc-10660752.title: Factors Affecting Thai Fathers’ Self-Efficacy to Support Exclusive Breastfeeding
pmc-10660752.creator: Preeyakamon Krikitrat, Nantaporn Sansiriphun, Jirawan Deeluea, Sirirat Sonted, Wongduean Chaiwipassatorn, Daniel Bressington
pmc-10660752.description: Background: Breastfeeding is the ideal approach for feeding infants and is an important public health consideration. Successful exclusive breastfeeding initiation and duration is influenced by fathers’ support. Paternal self-efficacy to support breastfeeding has also been shown to mediate infant feeding practices. The aim of this study was to investigate factors associated with Thai fathers’ self-efficacy to support maternal exclusive breastfeeding.

pmc-11644319.title: Excitation-Dependent pKa Extends the Sensing Range of Fluorescence Lifetime pH Sensors
pmc-11644319.creator: Emily P Haynes, Mary Canzano, Mathew Tantama
pmc-11644319.description: Biological activity is strongly dependent on pH, which fluctuates within a variety of neutral, alkaline, and acidic local environments. The heterogeneity of tissue and subcellular pH has driven the development of sensors with different pKa values, and a huge assortment of fluorescent sensors have been created to measure and visualize pH in living cells and tissues.

pmc-11664483.title: Bidirectional links between sleep and pain among heavy-drinking veterans with insomnia
pmc-11664483.creator: Eunjin Lee Tracy, Christine J So, Sydney D Shoemaker, Jill A Kanaley, Timothy Trull, Camila Manrique-Acevedo, Christina S McCrae, Brian Borsari, Mary Beth Miller
pmc-11664483.description: Study ObjectivesMilitary veterans often suffer from chronic pain and sleep issues at a greater frequency than the general population, leading some to self-medicate with alcohol. While research shows a connection between sleep and pain, few studies have examined bidirectional links between sleep and pain at the daily level—or the extent to which alcohol use may moderate these associations.

pmc-13209044.title: Synergistically Reinforced Copper-Free Friction Materials with Agricultural Wastes and Carbon Fibers: Evaluation of Tribological Performance
pmc-13209044.creator: Yitong Tian, Kunsen Huang, Zihe Xu, Yuqi Zhuansun, Yunhai Ma
pmc-13209044.description: Driven by global environmental regulations that strictly limit copper content in brake pads, traditional copper-based friction materials face significant challenges due to their negative ecological impacts. Consequently, the development of sustainable, copper-free alternatives has become an inevitable trend in the braking industry.

pmc-13447457.title: External validation of established clinical risk scores for cancer-associated venous thromboembolism in a Brazilian registry
pmc-13447457.creator: Márcia Fayad Marcondes de Abreu, Mohamad Al Bannoud, Sandra Martins, Stephany C. Huber, Beatriz de Moraes Martinelli, Maria Carmen GL Fernandes, Júlio C Teixeira, José BC Carvalheira, Carmen SP Lima, Nelson A Andreollo, Maurício Etchebehere, Lair Zambon, Ubirajara Ferreira, Alfio José Tincani, Antôn
pmc-13447457.description: Cancer-associated thrombosis (CAT) is a relevant cause of morbidity and mortality in oncology patients. Although several venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk assessment models (RAMs) are recommended to guide thromboprophylaxis in ambulatory cancer patients, their performance varies across populations. Data from Brazilian cohorts are limited, and the real-world performance of these models in this setting remains unclear.

pmc-13507344.title: Competition in the brain: a conserved principle with lifespan consequences
pmc-13507344.creator: Dipanjan Roy, Arpan Banerjee
pmc-13507344.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Whole-brain models have long assumed purely cooperative brain connectivity, but Luppi et al. demonstrate that competitive couplings are a conserved feature of the mammalian connectome, markedly improving model accuracy across humans, macaques, and mice. This Comment examines the lifespan implications — from adolescent maturation of long-range competitive connections to their erosion in aging and neurodegeneration — and the framework’s translational potential for personalised brain models and clinical biomarkers.

pmc-13530162.title: Dual-function floating-gate memory driver for energy-efficient integrated display–illumination system
pmc-13530162.creator: Haifeng Wu, Yizhe Wang, Qijun Zong, Jiali Yi, Huawei Liu, Xingxia Sun, Qin Shuai, Jian Hu, Xiao Lin, Yazhou Wang, Penghui Guo, Xudong Yang, Tanghao Xie, Xiaoqin Liao, Ben Wang, Xiaoming Zhao, Xiaoli Zhu, Bobo Tian, Xiao Wang, Dong Li, Anlian Pan
pmc-13530162.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The increasing demand for multifunctional micro-displays capable of both high-brightness illumination and low-power image display highlights a critical bottleneck in existing display technologies, which struggle to efficiently switching between large-area uniform light output and fine-grained pixel-level control. Here, we introduce the Integrated Nonvolatile Display–Illumination System (INDIS)—a monolithically integrated Micro-LED architecture based on transparent indium tin oxide (ITO) floating-gate memory (FGM) devices, achieving dual-mode operation.

pmc-13644094.title: Trehalose priming enhances chromium resilience in barley plants by modulating antioxidant defense, hormonal balance, endogenous trehalose, and nutrient homeostasis
pmc-13644094.creator: Adeeba Zafar, Muhammad Umer Chattha, Imran Khan, Muhammad Bilal Chattha, Jameel M Al-Khayri, Othman Al-Dossary, Bader Alsubaie, Mohammed I Aldaej
pmc-13644094.description: BackgroundCr stress represents a major threat to ecosystem sustainability, crop productivity, and human health. Tre is a non-reducing sugar with significant potential to alleviate abiotic stress toxicity. However, its role in mitigating Cr toxicity via seed priming remains poorly understood.

pmc-13687132.title: Comparative palatability and efficacy of two praziquantel isomers in rainbow trout infected by eyefluke
pmc-13687132.creator: Shilu Huang, Kaan Kumas, Kurt Buchmann
pmc-13687132.description: Praziquantel is a widely used anthelmintic in both human and veterinary medicine, but low palatability of the commonly used compound, which is a mixture (M) of two isomers (D and L forms), may result in rejection of oral treatments. Purification of the D-isomer of praziquantel allows a comparative evaluation of both palatability and efficacy of the isomers.
